newsitem.title: SHARJAH: CRICKET-MORRISON'S DREAM SPELL GRABS TIE FOR NEW ZEALAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MORRISON'S DREAM SPELL GRABS TIE FOR NEW ZEALAND.

text.p: Danny Morrison produced a dream spell to help New Zealand tie the match against world champions Sri Lanka in the Singer Champions Trophy cricket tournament on Monday.

In the dramatic 48th over, with Sri Lanka needing just one run to win with two wickets in hand, Morrison first cleaned bowled Sajeeva de Silva with this third delivery and then had Muttiah Muralitharan caught by Stephen Fleming in the slips on his last ball.
The tie -- both teams scored 169 -- was a tribute to the compelling comeback of New Zealand.

Sri Lanka looked well on course for victory, despite a middle order collapse when they were 98 for six in 29 overs. They built their innings around flamboyant opener Sanath Jayasuriya, who scored a vibrant 53 in 66 balls with five fours while skipper Arjuna Ranatunga weighed in with a patient 34 off 71 balls with four fours.
When Ranatunga left, Sri Lanka needed 11 runs to win with two wickets and 28 balls in hand.
But their tail-enders cracked under tremendous pressure. Man of the match Danny Morrison returned with a haul of five 34 in 10 overs.

Earlier, New Zealand, batting first after winning the toss, owed much to Nathan Astle (66 off 130 balls with three fours and one six) after medium pacer Sajeeva de Silva got rid of Craig Spearman and Adam Parore off successive balls in his third and the team's sixth over.
Astle paced his innings with maturity in the face of a spot-on attack by the Sri Lankans, their medium pacers in particular working up a lively pace on a helpful wicket.
The fall of Stephen Fleming and Chris Cairns added to New Zealand's woes.

With New Zealand four down for 61 in 22.4 overs, Astle, together with a subdued Mark Greatbatch, stemmed the rot to some extent with a stand of 75 for the fifth wicket. Greatbatch scored 35 off 58 balls, all in singles and twos.

When Astle fell to a brilliant catch by Roshan Mahanama in the 42nd over, New Zealand had crawled to 136. With the team fast running out of overs, the lower order batsmen failed to raise the tempo of the game they needed badly to post to a challenging total.
